components.name: Stat Plate
components.description: Data readout plate inside the cream For-Agents panel.

narrative.overview: The page is a large railway station: the first viewport is one wall-sized mechanical split-flap board in a matte anodized frame, and every section below is station furniture — laminated transfer signs, dual departures panels, an engineering schematic, a timetable. The metaphor is load-bearing: each knowledge domain is a departure line, each document count is real timetable data, and the standing status is ON TIME. Amber is the single working voice on warm near-black; cream is the touchable paper of signage; red exists only where data signals severity. Density is the aesthetic — ~220 tiles fill the first viewport and one slot mechanically re-flips every 4.2 seconds so the board reads as alive.
keyCharacteristics: Split-flap tile as atomic unit: 3px radius, 2px mid-seam, inset bevels, amber mono glyphs
Data-first hero — timetable rows are the pitch, never a centered hero triad
One accent (amber), one alert (red), one paper (cream) on warm near-black #0E0E0D
Monospace reserved for code, data and measurement
Station vocabulary: 线路 / 换乘 / ON TIME / DEPARTED / BOARDING

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Amber is the only accent; red appears only where the data itself signals severity, never as decoration.

rules.name: The Measurement Voice Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for code, data and measurement; narrative text is never set in mono.

rules.name: The Machine-In-Wall Rule
rules.body: The board is inset into darkness; cards lift softly off it. Shadows always carry blur; nothing is stamped.

dos: Do compose any new data surface from split-flap tiles (3px radius, mid-seam, amber mono glyphs).
Do keep every number real and traceable to the repo — scale is the pitch.
Do use station vocabulary for states and sections.
Do theme browser surfaces: amber selection on ink, tile favicon, theme-color #0E0E0D.
Do ship a full prefers-reduced-motion downgrade.
donts: Don't put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading — the heading carries its own weight.
Don't use zero-blur offset shadows — this world is inset and lifting, never stamped.
Don't introduce a second accent; red is reserved for severity data.
Don't set narrative text in monospace or use a system display face.
Don't drift the ground toward blue-black slate or warm cream page fields.
Don't invent metrics, testimonials or customer logos.
